Beginner Guide: How This Call Trade Works in Plain Dollars

Why this spread works differently from buying shares: DOCN pulled back into its major $67.44 support shelf while Pass 1 confirmed COMPOUNDER_PASS fundamentals — even though Stage 2 equity rules wait for trend repair, a defined-risk Bull Call Spread captures a rebound with strictly capped downside.

Exact wallet math (1 contract = 100 shares): You buy the $85 Call for $12.50 and simultaneously sell the $100 Call for $7.10, paying $5.40/sh net ($540.00 total for 1 spread(s)). That $540.00 is the absolute maximum you can lose.

Breakeven & profit ceiling: At expiry (2027-01-15), you start making money above $90.40 (+4.7% from $86.32). Anywhere at or above $100, your $540.00 turns into $1,500.00 (+$960.00 net profit).

Speed & time decay in plain English: Today, each $1 move up in DOCN adds ~$18.70 to your spread (Net Delta), while sitting flat costs ~$0.16/day in time decay (Net Theta) — much lower than an unhedged call because the sold $100 call decays in your favor.
